contrapunto-parametros.texto:
I'll compute the Bayesian Knowledge Tracing posterior for each technician, starting from P(L0)=0.10, with P(T)=0.12, P(G)=0.15, P(S)=0.10.

For each observation: if correct, posterior = P(L)(1−S) / [P(L)(1−S) + (1−P(L))G]; if incorrect, posterior = P(L)S / [P(L)S + (1−P(L))(1−G)]. Then apply learning: P(L) ← posterior + (1−posterior)·0.12.

Key values: a correct answer from a prior of 0.10 gives about 0.43 posterior; an incorrect answer gives about 0.012. Each step's learning adds roughly 0.12 of the remaining mass.

T01 (all ✗): the posterior stays very low, around 0.2 at most. Not mastered.

T02 (✗✗✗✓✓✓✓✓): five consecutive correct answers after an early streak of errors push mastery well above 0.95? Working through the recurrence: after the ✓ at position 4, P(L) is about 0.43 then roughly 0.5 after learning; after the subsequent ✓s it rises to about 0.92, then about 0.97 by the fifth ✓. Ending posterior after the final correct answer is around 0.97.

T03 (all ✗): same as T01, far from mastery.

T04 (✗✗✗✗✗✗✓✓): two correct answers at the end. Starting near 0.02 after six errors, the first ✓ gives about 0.20 and the second about 0.50 after the posterior and learning are combined. Not at 0.95.

T05 (✗✗✗✓✓✓✓✓): same pattern as T02, ending near 0.97.

T06 (✗✗✗✓✗✗✓✓): one early ✓ then errors drive mastery back down; the final two ✓s bring it to roughly 0.6–0.7. Not mastered.

T07 (all ✗ except last ✓): one correct answer from a low prior gives about 0.1–0.2. Not mastered.

T08 (✗✓✓✓✓✓✓✓): seven consecutive correct answers after one error; mastery climbs to above 0.99.

T09 (✗✓✓✓✓✓✓✓): identical sequence to T08, above 0.99.

T10 (✗✓✓✓✓✗✓✓): a single error at position 6 after a strong run only modestly lowers the posterior, and the final two ✓s restore it above 0.95.
